name: Gain cross-section and thermo-optic constants of Yb:YAG measured from 80 to 300 K in an LN2-cooled vacuum cryostat
plain_name: Measure how a laser crystal's light amplification changes as it is cooled from room temperature to 80 K
description: Mukhin et al. (IAP RAS) braze a 0.3 mm Yb:YAG crystal to a copper plate in a vacuum cryostat with a liquid-nitrogen-cooled vessel, pump it at ~938 nm through an optical window and record luminescence spectra and thermo-optic constants between 80 and 300 K.
keywords: Measure how a laser crystal's light amplification changes as it is cooled from room temperature to 80 K

sources.citation: Laser and thermal characteristics of Yb:YAG crystals in the 80-300 K temperature range (Mukhin et al., Quantum Electronics 41(11) 1045-1050, 2011)

reported_equipment: vacuum chamber with a liquid nitrogen-cooled vessel

requirements.rationale: Spectral and thermo-optical characteristics were measured across 80-300 K.
The cryostat was a vacuum chamber in which the crystal is conductively cooled.
The pump beam enters and the luminescence leaves through an optical window.
Optional: the source cryostat used a liquid-nitrogen-cooled vessel.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
